newsitem.title: USA: Initial jobless claims up in latest week.
newsitem.headline: Initial jobless claims up in latest week.

text.p: The number of Americans lining up to collect first-time jobless benefits climbed last week, the Labour Department said Thursday.
The department said initial claims in the week ended Jan. 18 rose to 355,000 from a revised 321,000 in the previous week.
Wall Street economists had forecast initial jobless claims at 347,000 for last week.
The less volatile four-week moving average, which is viewed as a more accurate barometer of the labour market, rose to 353,750 last week from a revised 351,000 the previous week.
The total number of Americans claiming benefits in the week ended Jan. 11, the latest period for which data were available, fell to about 2.48 million from 2.58 million the week earlier.
The department said 29 states and Puerto Rico reported increases in claims exceeding 1,000 on an unadjusted basis in the week ended Jan. 11, the latest period for which data were available.

Among the largest were Ohio, with 11,329 new claims filings; North Carolina, with 11,269; Georgia, with 11,085; Tennessee, with 10,644; Pennsylvania, with 8,432; Illinois, with 7,781; and Alabama, with 7,086.

Ohio attributed the increase to holiday shutdowns in various industries. North Carolina had layoffs in the textile, apparel, furniture, rubber, non-electrical machinery and electrical equipment industries.
Labour said four states reported decreases in initial claims exceeding 1,000, unadjusted, in the Jan. 11 week.

They were New York, with 11,966 fewer filings; Michigan, with 8,365; Arkansas, with 3,155; and Indiana, with 1,265. Michigan reported fewer layoffs in a variety of industries, while Arkansas had fewer layoffs in the non-electrical machinery industry.
